build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player can transform between three distinct forms (cube, sphere, triangle or equivalent) using button presses. Each form has visibly different physics: one is heavy/grippy, one is bouncy/elastic, one is light/floaty. Transformation is instant and works mid-air. Score 0 if fewer than 3 forms exist or transformation is not possible.
The heavy form activates pressure plates and breaks fragile floors. These interactions are exclusive to this form — other forms cannot trigger them. Score 0 if no form-specific interactions exist.

The bouncy form ricochets off walls and surfaces, gaining height with each bounce. This form reaches elevated areas that other forms cannot access through normal jumping. Score 0 if no bounce mechanic exists.
The gliding form floats across wide horizontal gaps that other forms cannot cross. Gliding has limited duration or gradual descent, requiring timing. Score 0 if no glide mechanic exists.

Puzzles require chaining transformations mid-air — launching as one form, switching to another mid-arc, and landing as a third. At least one level demonstrably requires a mid-air form switch to complete. Score 0 if all puzzles can be solved with a single form.
At least 20 levels are present across 4 worlds. Each world focuses on teaching and then combining form abilities. Levels have unique puzzle layouts. Score 0 if fewer than 10 levels exist.

Worlds introduce forms progressively: World 1 teaches the heavy form, World 2 the bouncy form, World 3 the gliding form, World 4 combines all three. Each world has distinct puzzle elements tied to its form. Score 0 if all forms are available from the start with no teaching progression.

Optional collectible stars (at least 1 per level) reward creative form usage or difficult sequences. Stars are not required for progression but track completion percentage. Score 0 if no optional collectibles exist.

Environmental puzzle elements (pressure plates, fragile floors, updrafts, bounce surfaces, wide gaps) are present and require specific forms to interact with. At least 4 distinct puzzle element types exist. Score 0 if no environmental puzzle elements exist.
Level completion shows time, stars collected, and form-switch count. A world-select screen shows overall progress and star totals. Score 0 if no completion tracking exists.
A styled title screen shows the three forms and the game name with thematic art. A world-select menu is accessible. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The game flow connects title -> world select -> level -> completion -> back to select without restarting. Score 0 if transitions are missing.

During gameplay, the current form is indicated in the HUD, and form-switch buttons or indicators show available transformations. The goal crystal and collectible stars are clearly visible. Score 0 if no form indicator exists.
Readability at 1280x720 is strong: all three forms are visually distinct, puzzle elements are clearly identifiable by type, and the goal is obvious. Score 0 if forms or elements blend together.

The art direction is coherent across title, worlds, forms, puzzle elements, and UI — a consistent colorful puzzle-platformer aesthetic. Score 0 if mostly default UI or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

The three forms have distinct, polished sprite art with visible personality. Transformation produces a satisfying visual morph animation. Environments use real tile art per world theme. Score 0 if forms are plain colored shapes or environments are uniform fills.

HUD and UI chrome: form indicator, world select, level complete screen, and star display use styled themed widgets — not raw unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if primary UI elements are obviously unstyled.

Animation and feedback: form transformation has a morph effect, bouncing produces squash-and-stretch, gliding shows wind particles, pressure plates depress visibly, and level completion has a celebratory animation. Score 0 if all state changes snap silently.
